name: App API health + survivability
purpose: keeps the App API from silently disappearing (the 2026-10-31 regression where a reboot cleared the /data/local/tmp staging copy and nobody noticed the runtime was down). On boot and on a timer it (1) verifies the runtime service (unit app-api, 127.0.0.1:3411) is up and re-stages it from the chroot if the loopback service died, (2) checks the ban-safe read path (launcher notification access) and the on-demand capture units, (3) fires a PowOS notification + a board task if the runtime - the part that must always be up - is down or gone. Health check only; it does NOT start capture, push frida, or install the CA (those stay user-gated).
installedBy: targets/android/rooted/powos-deploy.sh (health-check.sh staged with tools/app-api by rooted.sh deploy); scheduled by powos-start.sh at session start
selinux: unchanged - a read-only shell check run as the powos user; no policy change, no permissive
lifecycle: runs once at session/boot start and every 10 min; exits non-zero only when the runtime service is down

checks.runtime: curl 127.0.0.1:3411/apps answers (FAIL -> notify + board task + restart service app-api)
checks.read_path: launcher holds notification access (the needs-me read path); WARN if revoked
checks.capture_units: app-frida / app-ca presence reported as info, not failure (default resting state is absent)

remove.note: removing the script stops the health check; the runtime (unit app-api) is unaffected.
